Name: AGRC: Improve rice management
Description (SISEPUEDE): Reduce CH4 emissions from rice production by 45% due to improved management and reduced flooding.
CPAT base it acts on: Rice methane (agricultural CH4 x CPAT rice share)

Name: AGRC: Decrease demand for unhealthy crops
Description (SISEPUEDE): Reduction in demand for specified crops; the default is sugarcane.

Name: AGRC: Decrease Exports
Description (SISEPUEDE): Decrease agricultural exports by 50% (relative to final time period)

Name: AGRC: Reduce supply chain losses
Description (SISEPUEDE): Reduce waste food waste in the agricultural (crop) supply chain (pre-consumer)

Name: AGRC: Expand conservation agriculture
Description (SISEPUEDE):
| Decrease soil organic carbon loss in croplands and leave crop residues (reduce fraction removed and burned)
 | 
 | **Croplands**: Increases :math:`F_{MG}` for ``croplands`` to 1.067 (see V4, Chapter 5, Table 5.5 [2019R] for croplands management factors :math:`F_{MG}` under different management regimes--mean of *No-Till*)

Name: AGRC: Increase residue removal
Description (SISEPUEDE): Unlike conservation agriculture, remove residues from croplands. However, does not coincide with no till agriciulture.

Name: LNDU: Bound Classes
Description (SISEPUEDE): Land use classes are estimated using a transition matrix and ajdusted using a quadratic program. This transformation can be used to set upper and lower bounds on transitionable land use classes. This transformation can be used to represent the addition of protected areas through the use of a minimum bound OR the prevention of additional growth through the maxium bound.

Name: LNDU: Stop deforestation
Description (SISEPUEDE): Halt deforestation of primary and secondary forests

Name: LNDU: Decrease loss of land use classes
Description (SISEPUEDE): Halt loss of a specified land use class; similarly to DEC_DEFORESTATION, it increases the probability of a class transitioning into itself. The DEC_DEFORESTATION transformer, however, prevents multiple classes from transitioning out.

Name: LNDU: Expand sustainable grazing practices
Description (SISEPUEDE):
| Decrease soil organic carbon loss in grasslands through sustainable grazing practices
 | 
 | **Grasslands**: Increase :math:`F_{MG}` for ``grasslands`` to 1.157 (see V4, Chapter 6, Table 6.2 [2019R] for grasslands management factors :math:`F_{MG}` under different management regimes--mean of *Improved Grassland*)

Name: LNDU: Increase Reforestation
Description (SISEPUEDE): Increases probability of input land use classes being converted to secondary forests. This transformation can be defined for specific land use classes--e.g., converting only shrublands and croplands to

Name: LNDU: Expand silvopasture
Description (SISEPUEDE): Increase the use of silvopasture by increaasing the average sequestration factor associated with pastures. This transformer models silvopasture as a fraction of pastures with planted forests. Since the magnitude is a fraction of area, the average sequestration factor is estimated as m*f, where m is the magnitude (prevalence) and f is the secondary forest sequestration factor.

Name: LNDU: Partial land use reallocation
Description (SISEPUEDE): Set land use reallocation factor to 0.5

Name: LSMM: Increase biogas capture at anaerobic decomposition facilities
Description (SISEPUEDE): Increase the fraction of biogas that is captured at manure treated at anaerobic livestock manure treatment facilities

Name: LSMM: Improve manure management for cattle and pigs
Description (SISEPUEDE):
| 95% of manure from cattle (dairy and non-dairy) and pigs is treated. Under default conditions, the manure treated is sent to the following pathways:
 |    37.5% to Anaerobic Digestion
 |    12.5% to Composting
 |    25.0% to Daily Spread
 |    12.5% to Deep Bedding
 |    12.5% to Solid Storage

Name: LSMM: Improve manure management for other animals
Description (SISEPUEDE):
| 95% of manure from all other animals is treated. The manure treated is sent to the following pathways:
 |    37.5.% to Composting
 |    12.5% to Dry Lot
 |    25.0% to Daily Spread
 |    25.0% to Solid Storage

Name: LSMM: Improve manure management for poultry
Description (SISEPUEDE):
| 95% of manure from poultry (chickens) and pigs is treated. The manure treated is sent to the following pathways:
 |    100% to Poultry Management

Name: LVST: Decrease exports
Description (SISEPUEDE): Decrease exports of livestock and livestock products by 50% (relative to final time period)

Name: LVST: Increase livestock productivity
Description (SISEPUEDE): Increase inferred livestock carrying capacity by 20%

Name: SOIL: Improve fertilizer application
Description (SISEPUEDE): Decrease total nitrogen applied  through more precise fertilizer use (default 5%)

Name: WASO: Consumer food waste reduction
Description (SISEPUEDE): Reduce the amount of food waste generated per capita

Name: WASO: Decrease average landfill methane correction factor
Description (SISEPUEDE): Specify a fractional reduction in the average methane correction factor at landfills. Can be used to represent shifts to semi-aerobic landfills. Negative values will _increase_ the MCF, representing a shift to anaerobic landfills.

Name: WASO: Increase composting and biogas
Description (SISEPUEDE): Increase the fraction of yard, food, and sludge waste that is treated by anaerobic digesters or compost

Name: WASO: Increase biogas capture
Description (SISEPUEDE): Increase fraction of biogas captured from landfills and anaerobic digesters

Name: WASO: Biogas for energy production
Description (SISEPUEDE): Increase the fraction of biogas that is collected that is used for energy

Name: WASO: Increase landfilling
Description (SISEPUEDE): Increase fraction of waste that is otherwise untreated (i.e., post recycling, composting, etc.) that is sent to landfills

Name: CCSQ: Increase direct air capture
Description (SISEPUEDE): Increase Direct Air Capture deployment to 50 MT CO2e by final time period.

Name: ENFU: Adjust Exports
Description (SISEPUEDE): Increase OR Decrease exports of fuels

Name: ENTC: Reduce transmission losses
Description (SISEPUEDE): Decrease transmission losses by upgrading electrical transmission infrastructure.

Name: ENTC: Clean hydrogen
Description (SISEPUEDE): Set a target for clean hydrogen production.

Name: ENTC: 95% of electricity is generated by renewables in final time period
Description (SISEPUEDE): Set a target for renewable electricity. Includes minimum targets for specific renewable energy technologies.

Name: INEN: Fuel switch high- and low-temp thermal processes
Description (SISEPUEDE): Transformations for both (and/or) low and high-heat should be implemented using this transformer.

Name: SCOE: Reduce end-use demand for heat energy by improving building shell
SCOE: Switch to electricity for heat using heat pumps, electric stoves, etc.
TRNS: Increase electric transportation energy efficiency
TRNS: Increase non-electric transportation energy efficiency
TRNS: Increase occupancy for private vehicles
TRNS: Electrify light duty road transport
TRNS: Fuel switch medium duty road transport
CPAT base it acts on: Road diesel (medium and heavy duty, upper bound)

Name: TRNS: Mode shift freight
Mapping: M:1; gap (no mode choice in CPAT)

Name: TRNS: Mode shift passenger vehicles to others
Mapping: M:1; gap (no mode choice in CPAT)

Name: TRNS: Mode shift regional passenger travel
Mapping: M:1; gap (no mode choice in CPAT)

Name: IPPU: Reduce cement clinker
Description (SISEPUEDE): Reduces use of clinker in cement production

Name: IPPU: Reduce other fluorinated compounds
Description (SISEPUEDE): Includes SF6, NF3, HCFCs, and others

Name: PFLO: Change diets
Description (SISEPUEDE): Includes a reduction in the demand for red meat and allows for changes to different crop demands.
CB transformation-cost items [multiplier: cb:pflo:human_health:better_diets:X [350 $/person with better diet]; cb:pflo:consumer_savings:better_diets:X [385 $/person with better diet]

Name: PFLO: Industrial carbon capture and sequestration
Description (SISEPUEDE): Implements carbon capture at industrial facilities, affecting both INEN and IPPU emissions. Specify a minimum target fraction of industrial facilities using carbon capture (prevalence) and target effectiveness of carbon capture at those faciltiies.
CPAT base it acts on: Fossil fuel in iron and steel, cement, chemicals
